top_story.headline: Kalshi hires Empire Consulting Group to lobby on prediction markets
top_story.dek: Empire Consulting Group registered for the prediction-market exchange and, the same day, for the Business Roundtable.
paragraphs: Empire Consulting Group filed a new LDA registration for Kalshi Inc., a regulated prediction market exchange, covering "issues related to prediction markets and finance" under the Commodities and Financial Institutions/Investments/Securities issue areas. The filing lists former congressional staff as covered positions, including a former chief of staff to Rep. Robin Kelly and a former senior advisor to Rep. Gregory Meeks. Its Business Roundtable registration lists Michael Hayes, a former deputy director of the White House Office of Public Engagement and former National Security Council director.

A second new registration, for Innovation Council Action Inc. (super intelligence infrastructure and regulation), lists Nicholas Elliot, whose filed covered positions include senior advisor at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on a White House detail. Neither filing shows contact with the President, the Vice President or a cabinet official.
No FARA filing or OGE ethics filing in this window involved the President, Vice President or cabinet. The Senate disclosure feed failed to load today, so Senate filings were not checked.

paragraphs: No FARA filing in the window showed a communication with the President, Vice President or a cabinet member. One LDA report names two cabinet-level officials in its listing.

items: National Small Business Association (in-house, 3rd Quarter report): the filing names Kelly Loeffler and Lori Chavez-DeRemer. The lobbying description shown is the Corporate Transparency Act (31 U.S.C. 5336) and beneficial-ownership disclosure. LDA report.

sections.headline: No new ethics agreements or divestitures filed
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics received 16 filings in the monitoring window ending October 27, all of which had been previously reported.

sections.headline: Three House filings, one stock-trade report with eight small trades
paragraphs: Three House filings were new in this window: a new-filer report, a candidate report and one periodic transaction report. The Senate eFD feed returned an unreadable response, so no Senate filings were checked.

items: Jordan Smith Maggio (NY-01): new-filer report, filed October 28, 2026. Filing.
Ron Charles Russell (ME-01): candidate report, filed October 29, 2026. Filing.

Rep. David J. Taylor (OH-02): periodic transaction report filed October 29, 2026, listing eight transactions, all dated October 15 and each in the $1,001 to $15,000 range. There are five purchases (AT&T Inc., Lam Research Corporation, Prologis, Inc. twice, RPM International Inc.) and three sales (Marathon Petroleum Corporation twice, Visa Inc.). The filing came 14 days after the trades, within the 45-day STOCK Act window, so none is marked late. Filing.
